prompt:
You are a formal verification assistant. The following Dafny program fails Dafny verification.

=== PROGRAM ===
// successfully verifies
method GetEven(a: array<nat>)
requires true;
ensures forall i:int :: 0<=i<a.Length ==> a[i] % 2 == 0
modifies a
{
    var i := 0;
    while i < a.Length
    invariant 0 <= i <= a.Length && forall j:int :: 0<=j< (i) - 1 ==> a[j] % 2 == 0
    decreases a.Length - i
    {
        if a[i] % 2 != 0
        {
            a[i] := a[i] + 1;
        }
        i := i + 1;
    }
}

=== DAFNY ERROR ===
program.dfy(8,4): Error: a postcondition could not be proved on this return path

program.dfy(4,8): Related location: this is the postcondition that could not be proved
  |
4 | ensures forall i:int :: 0<=i<a.Length ==> a[i] % 2 == 0
  |         ^^^^^^

program.dfy(9,36): Error: this invariant could not be proved to be maintained by the loop
 Related message: loop invariant violation

Dafny program verifier finished with 1 verified, 2 errors

=== COUNTEREXAMPLE ===
For the error at line 8: At initial state: a.Length = 1237, a[1236] = 3593. At a program state: i = 0.
For the error at line 9: At initial state: a.Length = 1238, a[1236] = 17891, a[1237] = 564. At a program state: i = 0.

Analyze the failure and respond with ONLY a valid JSON object — no explanation, no markdown, no code fences. Use exactly this structure:

{
  "spec_element": "<one of: requires | invariant | ensures>",
  "proof_obligation": "<one of: initiation | preservation | bridge>",
  "diagnosis": "<explanation of what broke and why>",
  "repair": "<the corrected Dafny specification line that restores the intended behavior>"
}

Definitions:
- requires: the precondition that must hold before the method executes
- invariant: the loop invariant that must hold throughout the loop
- ensures: the postcondition that the method must guarantee on return
- initiation: the precondition does not establish the invariant at loop entry
- preservation: the loop body does not maintain the invariant
- bridge: the invariant and loop exit condition do not imply the postcondition
raw_response: {"spec_element": "invariant", "proof_obligation": "preservation", "diagnosis": "The loop invariant bounds the quantifier with j < i - 1 instead of j < i, so it only covers the elements before a[i-1]. The body makes a[i] even and increments i. The new invariant then requires a[old i - 1] to be even, but the old invariant never covered that index, so preservation fails (counterexample: an odd element such as a[1236] = 17891). The same off-by-one leaves the last element a[a.Length-1] uncovered at loop exit, so the postcondition cannot be proved either (counterexample: a[1236] = 3593 with a.Length = 1237).", "repair": "invariant 0 <= i <= a.Length && forall j:int :: 0 <= j < i ==> a[j] % 2 == 0"}
reasoning_content:
The invariant condition j < i-1 is too weak since preservation would require j < i after the step, which includes j = i-1, an unverified case. There's also a bridge failure at the exit since the last element isn't covered, so I need to decide whether the preservation error or the postcondition bridge error is the one to flag as primary.

Both stem from the same root cause—the weak invariant. I'll call it the preservation failure, and the fix is to strengthen the invariant so that it bounds i correctly and asserts all elements before i are even.
